name: Chhattisgarhi

ancestors.notes: Descent from Old Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit); Eastern Hindi zone (Masica 1991).

Eastern Hindi group; shares Standard Hindi's Devanagari grapheme-to-sound conventions (schwa inherent vowel). Chhattisgarhi has no independent codified spelling norm distinct from Hindi's, hence graphemes_base=hi.

notes: Chhattisgarhi, spoken in Chhattisgarh, India. Eastern Hindi group (Masica 1991), distinct from the Bihari (Bhojpuri/Magahi/Maithili) group. Also historically written in Odia script in border areas; Devanagari is the official script (Chhattisgarh Official Language Act). Wikipedia phonology lists nasalisation as phonemically distinctive and a vowel inventory (iː uː ɪ ʊ eː ə oː ɛ ɔ aː) consistent with the standard Devanagari schwa-inherent-vowel reading used by Hindi, so no grapheme overrides are asserted pending a citable source describing divergent letter values.
